items.notes: #76: the only alternatives were the attack on a shieldless, baseless opponent with no Blocker, or end_main. Marida Cruz could not be paired. Attacking was correct; P1's Unforeseen Incident could not be foreseen.

findings.played: pair ST01-010 Amuro Ray with GD01-001 Gundam [59] (the unit already on the board); GD01-001 Gundam [79] was deployed from hand later (#52) with no pilot, so it could not attack
findings.better: deploy GD01-001 Gundam [79] first, then pair Amuro Ray with [79] (linked, so it can attack the turn it is deployed). This costs the same 4 resources and leaves the same final board, but [59] can still attack as well
findings.reason: The same cards and the same cost give one extra attack this turn: six attackers instead of five, against an opponent with 0 active resources and both Blockers rested. The same When Paired triggers (Amuro's rest, Gundam's draw) still happen. This would have given a spare attacker for the lethal line (Isaribi base, 3 shields, then the player).

findings.played: attack ST05-002 Gundam Barbatos 2nd Form [6] with GD04-008 Gundam [58]
findings.better: attack the player with GD04-008 Gundam, ST01-005 GM [83] and ST01-005 GM [90] (3 shields), then with GD01-004 Guncannon+Sleggar Law (the player)
findings.reason: After #48 destroyed the Isaribi base, P0 had 3 shields, no base, 0/6 active resources (no Action responses possible) and both Shiden Custom Blockers rested. Barbatos 4th, its only active unit, has no Blocker. P1 had exactly 4 active attackers: 3 to break the shields and 1 to hit the player. Only a Burst from the revealed shields could interfere. Instead, two attackers (GD04-008 here, Guncannon at #57) were spent on units, and P0 survived at 1 shield with 9 cards in hand.

items.notes: The order_trigger choices #46 and #61 were judged trivial. #49 (Unforeseen Incident on the rested Shiden Custom [8]) did have an effect: Guncannon later killed that unit and survived (#57). It was unnecessary in the lethal line, but it is not a separate finding. #57 came after lethal was already gone, so it is not judged as a separate finding.

findings.played: attack GD01-004 Guncannon with ST05-001 Gundam Barbatos 4th Form [48]
findings.better: attack the player with Barbatos 4th [48] (damaged, so it has <Suppression>: destroys 2 of the 3 shields), then with Barbatos 2nd Form [5] (last shield), then with Shiden Custom [26] (the player)
findings.reason: Gundam Flauros had just destroyed the Jaburo base. P1 had 3 shields, no base, 0/6 active resources, and its only active unit (Gundam [79]) has no Blocker. The setup this turn (Ryusei-Go damaging [48] for Suppression, Flauros+Akihiro to break the base) had built exactly this lethal. Only a shield Burst could interfere. Instead the AI traded into units and left P1 at 2 shields, while P0 sits at 1 shield facing a large board.

findings.played: attack the player with GD05-058 Shiden Custom [26] (P1: 3 -> 2 shields)
findings.better: end_main, keeping Shiden Custom active as P0's only <Blocker>, or trade it into the rested GD04-008 Gundam to remove one of P1's two attackers
findings.reason: P0 had 1 shield, no base and no other Blocker (Ryusei-Go [18] has none). P1 keeps Gundam [79] and GD04-008 for its next turn, exactly the two attacks it needs for lethal once Shiden is rested. P0 also has 0 active resources for Unforeseen Incident during P1's turn. Breaking one of P1's three shields gains nothing comparable to that risk.

items.notes: #62 to #68 (Ryusei-Go damaging Barbatos 4th for Suppression, Flauros destroying a GM, Akihiro linking Flauros, and Flauros breaking the base) were strong play. The #64 discard (Become a Shield) is a judgment call.

findings.played: play ST01-014 Unforeseen Incident during Core Booster's attack on the player, targeting ST03-006 Char's Zaku II (#71)
findings.better: pass and keep Unforeseen Incident (C1) for P1's turn. P0 would still have had 3 active resources then
findings.reason: AP-3 'during this turn' on an active enemy Unit, during P0's own turn, does nothing. Char's Zaku II is not in this battle and has no Blocker. It cannot be attacked while active, and P0 never used Jaburo's rest ability to set up an attack on it. P0 ends the turn at 1 shield plus Jaburo, facing Kshatriya AP5 and Char's Zaku II, and has thrown away its only defensive trick.

items.notes: #58 (Sleggar Law on Gundam (MA Form) for the draw, rather than on ST01-001 Gundam for its +1 AP aura) is arguable either way and is not reported. #64 Guntank had no rested target for its Deploy, but it still added a body. #74 end_main was correct: Jaburo's rest ability had no follow-up attacker.

findings.played: play ST01-014 Unforeseen Incident during Gundam's attack on the player, targeting P0's GD01-031 Gelgoog+Marida Cruz (AP6 -> 3 during this turn)
findings.better: pass and keep Unforeseen Incident (and the last active resource) for P0's turn
findings.reason: It is P1's own turn. Gelgoog is active, is not in the battle, has no Blocker and cannot be attacked, so an AP-3 that lasts only this turn changes nothing. Held, it could have shrunk Gelgoog's AP6 attack against one of P1's rested units on P0's turn.

items.notes: #33 (Guntank's Deploy finishing Zee Zulu) and #34/#35 (Guncannon plus Thoroughly Damaged as a linked pilot so it could attack) were good. #45 is a trivial Repair order.

#63: three attackers against 1 shield plus 1 Blocker (Shiden Custom) is lethal only with no tricks. P1 had 2 open resources and 3 hidden cards, and a shield Burst (AP-3 on Rick Dom [15]) stopped it. Close Combat on the rested Barbatos 1st Form (#65/#66) was good value. #69 end_main was correct: Rick Dom [15] had AP0, and Rick Dom [10] attacking would just die to the Shiden block with no lethal.

findings.played: play ST01-014 Unforeseen Incident during Barbatos 4th's attack on the player, targeting the rested GD03-001 Gundam NT-1 (#67)
findings.better: pass and keep Unforeseen Incident; P0 still had 4 active resources for P1's turn
findings.reason: NT-1 was not in the battle, and P0 had no attacker left this turn to send at it (Graze Custom and CGS were deployed this turn and cannot attack). AP-3 'during this turn' on it therefore did nothing, and the card was lost.

items.notes: Lethal was not available: only two attackers against Jaburo (5 HP) plus 2 shields. The AI's line was the maximum: Barbatos 1st broke the base, then Become a Shield gave Barbatos 4th <Suppression> to break both shields. Become a Shield's enemy target (GD04-008) is a judgment call.

findings.played: attack GD01-008 Guntank with GD01-031 Gelgoog+M'Quve (Breach 1 breaks the last shield), planning Zaku II (AP2, HP1) as the finisher
findings.better: attack the player with Zaku II first (breaks the last shield), then with Gelgoog AP5 as the finisher
findings.reason: Both lines are lethal barring a Burst. With the AP5, HP4 Gelgoog as the finisher, an AP-reduction Burst (Unforeseen Incident AP-3) or small damage would not stop it, whereas the AP2, HP1 Zaku finisher is stopped by either. Rest-type Bursts stop both lines. The AI's line gains a Guntank kill if lethal fails, so this is arguable. In the game a Burst on Zaku stopped lethal.

items.notes: #109 to #111 (Zanzibar first to fetch a second attacker, deploying Gelgoog free, M'Quve to link it) were correct. I assumed hand size is public; P0 had 0 cards.

findings.played: Mikazuki Augus's When Paired self-damage on Barbatos 1st Form [18] (and at #81, Barbatos 4th [17]'s Deploy damage also went to [18]), followed by a board-control line
findings.better: damage Barbatos 4th Form [11] instead (it gains <Suppression>). Then attack the player with [17]+Mikazuki AP6 (destroys Jaburo, 5 HP), [11] (Suppression destroys both shields) and Barbatos 1st [18] (the player)
findings.reason: P1 had no Blocker and all units but NT-1 rested, so three attacks would win. It is not certain: P1 held 2 open resources and 2 hidden cards (an Intercept Orders could rest the HP<=3 finisher), and 2 shield Bursts could interfere. A failed all-in at 1 shield would lose to P1's four units, while the control line actually taken (killing GD04-008, GD01-001 and GM) is defensible. Hence arguable.

items.notes: In the control line, #85/#88/#90 were sensible trades. #90 killing the GM (rather than hitting Jaburo) correctly reduced P1's attackers against P0's 1 shield.

findings.played: play ST03-012 Indignation (AP+2) on Gelgoog+M'Quve during its attack on GD01-008 Guntank
findings.better: pass, keeping Indignation (as a later combat trick or as the Angelo Sauper pilot)
findings.reason: Gelgoog's AP5 already destroys the 2 HP Guntank, and Breach deals a fixed 1. P1 had 0 active resources, so there was no AP-reduction to guard against. Gelgoog was P0's only attacker and is rested afterwards, so the +2 AP changed nothing and the card was lost.

items.notes: #41 (pairing M'Quve, the only Zeon-trait pilot, so the newly deployed Gelgoog is linked and can attack) was correct. #42's choice of the Guntank over the damaged GM is a judgment call.

findings.played: Unforeseen Incident (during GD01-004 Guncannon's attack on P0) targeting the non-attacking ST01-001 Gundam (AP4 -> 1)
findings.better: target the attacking GD01-004 Guncannon (AP3 -> 0, so this attack destroys no shield), or pass and hold the card
findings.reason: Any damage destroys a shield, so an AP1 Gundam still threatens a shield; the debuff bought nothing against shield attacks. Its only use, stopping the Gundam from killing the rested Barbatos 5th Form, was better done reactively: hold the card and play it if the Gundam attacked Barbatos, so the Gundam dies to Barbatos's 5 AP. Meanwhile the shield under attack was lost.

items.notes: #73 activating the Burst (Mikazuki Augus to hand) was correct.

#30/#31: Unforeseen Incident on the battling Rick Dom prevented 3 damage to Barbatos 2nd Form, keeping it out of range of Gelgoog/Char's Zaku on P1's turn. That is a reasonable use. Isaribi (#32) was the only remaining useful play.

#73: correct lethal attempt, with the weaker damaged Gundam first against 1 shield, no Blocker and an opponent holding 0 cards. A Zanzibar Burst stopped it. #75 (hitting the new base to 1 HP rather than trading GD04-008 for Sinanju) is a judgment call. #76 to #78 deployed everything.
